title: First-frame fidelity
rationale: The production path that matters most: art-direct a still, then animate it. Measures how much of the approved frame survives contact with the video model.
prompt: Animate the supplied style frame. The subject breathes and shifts weight; a curtain moves in the background. Nothing else changes. The first frame of the output must match the supplied frame.

variants.prompt: Animate the supplied style frame. A light wind moves the subject's hair and clothing; the subject holds their pose and the camera is still. The first frame of the output must match the supplied frame.
Animate the supplied style frame. The subject slowly turns their head toward the camera and smiles. Nothing else moves. The first frame of the output must match the supplied frame.
Animate the supplied style frame. The camera pushes in slowly toward the subject's face; the subject stays still. The first frame of the output must match the supplied frame.
Animate the supplied style frame. A cloud passes and the light dims, then returns. The subject and camera do not move. The first frame of the output must match the supplied frame.
Animate the supplied style frame. The subject stands and walks out of frame to the right; the empty room stays exactly as it was. The first frame of the output must match the supplied frame.

rubric: Does frame one match the supplied frame?
Is the composition still the approved composition at the end?
Is the added motion the motion requested and no more?
Does colour and grade drift across the clip
